data.body:
GAP 5 CALL-SITE SURVEY — the fix shape is now settled on evidence. All five finalize_verdict call
sites enumerated and each checked for whether a runner-assembled provenance record is REACHABLE.

  A workflow_ops.py:223   DET short-circuit          NO LLM RAN (coverage.llm_ran=False)
  B workflow_ops.py:759   plan_review_coach          the NORMAL happy path -- see below
  C plan_review_recovery.py:220  coach-failure recovery   REACHABLE: succeeded[STEP_VERIFY]
  D plan_review_recovery.py:284  verify-failure recovery  NOT reachable BY CONSTRUCTION
  E plan_review_recovery.py:321  outage degrade           NO LLM RAN (llm_unavailable=True)

THE KEY FINDING, which makes this a SMALL change rather than a large one. The verify step
(gates/plan-review.yaml:174) is an AGENT step, and RunnerAgentStep.run returns the runner result
VERBATIM as step outputs (workflow/runs.py:262). runner.py:533 already passes provider_provenance
into findings.finalize_outcome, which stamps it at findings.py:312-313,343-344. So
`${{ steps.verify.outputs.provider_provenance }}` ALREADY EXISTS and is simply never wired: the
coach step's `with:` block (plan-review.yaml:242-260 and the mirrored else arm at :262-278) wires
14 inputs and not that one. Site B is therefore ONE YAML WIRE plus one kwarg. Site C reads
succeeded[STEP_VERIFY]["provider_provenance"] (STEP_VERIFY = "verify", plan_review_recovery.py:37).

THE ROUTE I ALMOST TOOK AND MUST NOT: carrying provenance through coverage["usage"]. It is DROPPED,
and one layer EARLIER than expected. sizing.usage_record (sizing.py:272-290) builds each per-call
record from the runner result's `_usage` SUB-DICT only -- criteria + requests + the four token
fields (USAGE_TOKEN_FIELDS, sizing.py:264-269). provider_provenance lives at the TOP LEVEL of the
result, so it never enters the record; all five mint sites pass only the usage dict (pass1.py:253,
289, 384, 600; production_batch_runner.py:183). aggregate_usage (pass1.py:665-712) re-emits what it
is given and so would preserve the key, but cannot invent it. Going that way means changing
usage_record, every mint site, AND inventing a collapse rule for N-records-one-provenance. The
yaml wire gets the COMPLETE already-assembled record with none of that.

HONEST VALUE FOR THE THREE NO-RECORD SITES (A, D, E) -- a real design decision, recorded not
guessed. A and E ran NO model at all; D is the verify-failed path where succeeded[STEP_VERIFY] is
absent by construction. The temptation is to synthesize a record from cfg, since those sites
already report model=cfg.model. DO NOT: capabilities.provenance_for requires a resolved
ModelCapabilities describing what actually drove a run (capabilities.py:289-318) and its docstring
forbids recomputation precisely because a recomputed record can diverge from the one that ran. A
cfg-derived record at a site where nothing ran would reproduce the EXACT defect this record exists
to fix -- a verdict claiming a provider served it when none did. DECISION: omit the key. The
sidecar already tolerates absence (sidecar.py:630 uses .get; test_verdict_provenance.py:202,207 pin
that a legacy payload with no key loads and returns None).

THE SAME DEFECT EXISTS ON BOTH SIBLING GATES -- the ticket's "verify before assuming" was right:
  CODE REVIEW: finalize_code_review_verdict does verdict.setdefault("model", cfg.model) at
    finalize.py:244-245 and never sets provenance, while code_review/sidecar.py:106 reads it.
    Same cfg-derived shape, always None.
  COMPLETION: gate_ops.py:130-132 builds the verdict from ctx.inputs runner/model/trace_id, wired
    at completion-verification.yaml:66-68 from steps.verify.outputs. That verify step is ALSO an
    agent step, so its outputs already carry provenance -- the narrowest fix of the three, one more
    wired input. completion_sidecar.py:207,225 read a key the verdict never sets.

TWO PRE-EXISTING TEST DEFECTS FOUND, both worth their own attention (NOT fixed here):
 1. test_gate_dispatch_seam.py:47-55 guards gate_dispatch.py with the message "adding an argument at
    its three finalize_verdict call sites is not a build break" -- but after the 1484 split those
    three call sites live in plan_review_recovery.py. The test no longer guards the file it names.
    Its prose at :4 and plan_review_recovery.py:8 are stale the same way.
 2. Those seam tests reserve headroom in orchestrator.py (646, needs <700) and gate_dispatch.py
    (527) but assert NOTHING about plan_review/workflow_ops.py -- which holds TWO of the five call
    sites and sits at 787/800, THIRTEEN lines of headroom. The one file this change must edit is
    the one file no seam test protects. Site A needs no edit (the new kwarg defaults to None), so
    only site B's single line plus a short comment goes there; anything more must be extracted
    first.
